title: Cash for Europe trip.
body:
O.P.
Going to Europe with family of 4 in June. 5 Weeks. Accomodation atractions paid for will have credit card to pay for most things that you can with cc. How much cash should I exchange before leaving?

---- replies ----
[User #1763818231 postsTicTacToetrained chickenWhirlpool Forums Addict] Roswell writes...
How much cash should I exchange before leaving?
You don't really need cash much in Europe these days, and you can readily get cash from ATMs. You also can exchange AUD cash fairly easily. By all means get some to have an alternative means of payment available, but particularly if you have a debit card that doesn't charge FX fees, you can easily have a bit of AUD cash on you as your "just in case" safety net until you get over there and can take out local currency from an ATM.
What countries are you visiting?
[User #5805827047 postsB4dgerCaveat lector (8.5p,8i)Whirlpool Forums Addict] Roswell writes...
How much cash should I exchange before leaving? None. You might need some coins for parking if you are hiring a car and parking on the street in some places, and possibly need some cash for street vendors but mostly everything takes cards. You can take cash out at ATMs if you really need it.
[User #5151331264 postsuphillbattlerImprovise, adapt, overcomeWhirlpool Enthusiast] I took EUR200 cash last year. We loved the town markets in France in Italy and cash is king – and as above- ATMs are everywhere (use the bank ATMs) so we took out extra cash along the way. Cash is still widely used – eg – paying the tourist tax at AIRBNBs to the host on arrival – you pay in cash.

[User #1763818231 postsTicTacToetrained chickenWhirlpool Forums Addict] this post was edited
Roswell writes...
Paris, London, Greece, Rome.
You have little need for cash then, even in Greece where cash is used more, but cards are accepted in most situations.
Get a debit card without foreign transaction fees and take out small amounts as needed from ATMs – ideally ATMs attached to bank branches and just be on the lookout for scammy ATM tricks – ie. never ever accept AUD conversion in any circumstances, don't ask for your balance, be wary of options that specify "withdrawal and balance".
There was a time when I used to take cash before leaving but it's become increasingly difficult and more expensive to do so, so I have at least a couple of options for obtaining cash overseas, but I'm happy to depart Australia with a bit of AUD currency notes as my only cash for emergency backup.
See /wiki/international_atms for a wiki of people's experiences with ATM operator fees.
[User #2311071896 postsflyinfishfishin' the poolWhirlpool Enthusiast] Just back from Italy. You do need a small amount. Toilets at the train stations cost 1 euro, cash only. Markets, some shops, city tax, some taxis. ATMs as you need.
[User #6631513587 postsMarissaAnnaWhirlpool Forums Addict] Last year we flew in to Lisbon and taxi driver asked for cash. I think we took about 500 euros with us and were not stuck with it, we were in Spain and Malta as well. Southern Europe is still using some cash. Even a favourite Italian restaurant in southern Sydney is now offering 5% discount for cash and probably have the usual 1.5% credit card surcharge. You will find the same sort of situation at least in Italy and I would think in Greece.

[User #1763818231 postsTicTacToetrained chickenWhirlpool Forums Addict] Roswell writes...
I have a CBA Ultimate Rewards CC that has no foreign transaction fees.
Good for paying for things but not good for ATM withdrawals (because you don't get an interest-free period for cash withdrawals).
I also just applied yesterday for a CBA Travel card which has no transaction fees just in case I loose my CC and need to use it till the CC is replaced I can top that up within my netbank.
I like this product as a backup – but the correct way to use it is to only store AUD on it and (hopefully) never use it. Transferring some AUD onto the card as AUD is the only way to use it at no cost. When you get home, you can transfer that AUD back to your regular accounts and then it won't have cost you anything.
If you ever do need to use it, then a currency conversion will occur, and that conversion – like all travel money card products – will rip you off blind. But it's your emergency backup so you live with it in that situation.
Don't be tempted to store GBP or EUR on this card – then you guarantee the bank is ripping you off blind on the exchange.
[User #12354973968 postsMaccarossiPSN/XBL/Steam: MaccarossiWhirlpool Forums Addict] A bit of cash is handy if you need a toilet too, a lot of public toilets in Europe will have a fee so coins for that is handy.
[User #55247622923 postspedrovyes, I changed it....Whirlpool Forums Addict] Roswell writes...
also just applied yesterday for a CBA Travel card which has no transaction fees just in case I loose my CC
Is that your ATM card you are planning on using (should you need more cash)? If so, the conversion rate isn't good. Ok for a backup, but I wouldn't suggest doing much ATM withdrawals with it.
You want a debit card with no international fees AND doesn't charge their own conversion. Macquarie Debit card is about the easier/fastest to get hold of in short notice. You can use PayID/OSKO to transfer funds instantly between CBA and Macquarie, as needed.
